riskSection.headline: The compliance risk every company managing contractors faces
riskSection.body: When a company treats a worker as an independent contractor but that jurisdiction's employment law considers them an employee, the company is liable for back-taxes, unpaid social contributions, interest, and fines, often going back three years or more. Regulatory enforcement is active across Jackson & Frank's core markets.

callouts.title: IR35
callouts.description: HMRC holds the engaging company responsible for determining a contractor's employment status. If the determination is wrong, the company pays the shortfall in income tax and employer National Insurance, plus penalties.

callouts.title: Scheinselbstandigkeit
callouts.description: German pension insurance authorities (Deutsche Rentenversicherung) actively audit contractor arrangements. A finding of bogus self-employment triggers retroactive social security contributions from the engaging company.

callouts.title: URSSAF
callouts.description: France has one of the most proactive enforcement regimes in Europe. A reclassified contractor becomes a salaried employee with full retrospective employment rights, including paid leave entitlements and unfair dismissal protection.

riskSection.transition: As your Contractor of Record, Jackson & Frank assumes the compliance obligation. Your contractor is engaged through our local entity, the legal relationship sits with us, and our in-country team handles classification, contracts, and payments.

faqs.title: Common questions about Contractor of Record services

items.question: What is a Contractor of Record, and how is it different from an Employer of Record?
items.answer:
A Contractor of Record (COR) is a service where a third party, in this case Jackson & Frank, legally engages an independent contractor on your behalf through a local entity. The contractor remains an independent contractor; Jackson & Frank handles the compliance, contracts, and payments.

An Employer of Record (EOR) is different: an EOR engages someone as an employee, taking on full employer obligations including benefits, leave entitlements, and payroll taxes. EOR is the right structure when someone is working for you full-time and the working arrangement looks like employment. COR is the right structure when you genuinely want a contractor relationship but need the compliance handled correctly.

If you're not sure which applies to your situation, we'll tell you on the quote call.

items.question: How do you protect against contractor misclassification risk?
items.answer:
Misclassification happens when a company treats a worker as an independent contractor, but local employment law considers them an employee. The consequences include back-taxes, social contribution arrears, fines, and, in some jurisdictions, full employment rights backdated to the start of the relationship.

Jackson & Frank's in-country specialists review each working arrangement before a contract is issued. If the arrangement looks like employment under local law, we'll say so and recommend the appropriate structure. We don't issue COR agreements to arrangements that don't qualify, that would expose both Jackson & Frank and you.

items.question: Which markets do you cover for Contractor of Record services?
items.answer:
Jackson & Frank holds owned entities and in-country specialists in 17+ active markets: Belgium, China, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Hong Kong, India, Italy, Netherlands, Poland, Spain, UAE, and UK. Hungary, Portugal, Romania, and Sweden are coming soon.

If you're hiring contractors in a market not listed, get in touch, we may be able to support it. We'll confirm within 24 hours.

items.question: How does the 48-hour payment SLA work?
items.answer:
When you instruct Jackson & Frank to pay a contractor invoice, we process the payment within 48 hours. "Processing" means the payment has been initiated from Jackson & Frank's local account, clearing time after that depends on the receiving bank and the payment method, which varies by market.

You're invoiced by Jackson & Frank in your billing currency. We handle the local currency conversion and any local payment rails.

items.question: Can I use Jackson & Frank's Contractor of Record service in a market where I also directly employ staff?
items.answer: Yes. Many clients use Jackson & Frank for specific markets or specific contractor relationships while managing direct employment elsewhere. The two structures don't conflict. If you have an entity in one market and use Jackson & Frank for contractor management in a second market where you don't have an entity, that's a typical arrangement. For clients who engage contractors and also manage employees where they hold an entity, our payroll service covers that side of the workforce.

items.question: What happens if the contractor relationship needs to end?
items.answer: We handle offboarding through our local entity. This includes issuing formal notice in the format required by local law, final payment, and documentation. Independent contractor relationships typically have shorter notice obligations than employment contracts, but the requirements vary by market, our in-country team handles the local specifics.

items.question: Can you convert a contractor to a permanent employee?
items.answer: Yes, and we recommend reviewing whether this is appropriate when a contractor relationship has been running for an extended period, particularly in markets with strict classification rules (Germany, France, UK). Jackson & Frank's Employer of Record service can handle the conversion, the contractor transitions to an employee engaged through Jackson & Frank's local entity without you needing a local entity yourself.

items.question: What payment cycles and currencies do you support?
items.answer: We support monthly and bi-weekly payment cycles. Payments are made in the contractor's local currency, Jackson & Frank handles the exchange from your billing currency. If a contractor has specific payment timing requirements, discuss this during onboarding and we'll confirm whether it's accommodated in the relevant market.
